name: Amna Nawaz
description: Follow Amna Nawaz, a tracked person, in Lootura: recent changes, timeline, related context, and source-backed evidence.

changes.title: Ukraine less reliant on U.S. as Trump-Zelenskyy rift deepens, former ambassador says
changes.summary: For perspective on the tensions between President Trump and Ukrainian President Zelenskyy, Amna Nawaz spoke with former U.S. Ambassador to Ukraine William Taylor. He's now a distinguished fellow at the Atlantic Council.

changes.title: Pennsylvania doctor urges vaccination as measles outbreak grows
changes.summary: The CDC has confirmed more than 4,000 cases of measles this year as the country grapples with the largest outbreak of the highly infectious virus in 35 years. Nearly a fifth of cases comprise children under the age of five, and 95% are among unvaccinated people. Amna Nawaz spoke with Dr. Evan Shirey, a pediatric infect.

changes.title: How Starlink disruptions affected Ukraine's battlefield operations
changes.summary: A key component of Ukraine's communications network was partially disabled on Wednesday. The Starshield satellite network, funded by the Pentagon and operated by Elon Musk's SpaceX, was not operating at full capacity, hampering communications within the Ukrainian military. Liz Landers reports and Amna Nawaz discusses t.

changes.title: Economist breaks down new inflation report and what's driving prices higher
changes.summary: With the midterm elections just three weeks away, a new inflation report shows prices rising faster than expected, putting more pressure on Americans struggling with the cost of everyday essentials. To discuss what the latest numbers mean for Americans, Amna Nawaz spoke with Heather Long, vice president and chief econo.

changes.title: Trump Accounts expand to millions of children, but new rules raise questions
changes.summary: The Treasury Department has created Trump Accounts for every eligible child, automatically enrolling more than 60 million. The expansion also comes with changes to how the program works. Donors can now donate individual stocks that families can't choose or reject and must keep for five years. Amna Nawaz discussed more.

changes.title: Former U.S. ambassador on Saudi Arabia's struggle to defend against Houthi attacks
changes.summary: To discuss the escalating war between the Houthis in Yemen and Saudi Arabia, Amna Nawaz spoke with Michael Ratney. He served as U.S. ambassador to Saudi Arabia during the Biden administration and is now a senior adviser at the Center for Strategic and International Studies.

changes.title: Republican and Democratic strategists on closing messages and where they expect to win
changes.summary: Republicans hold a massive financial advantage, but it's Democrats making gains in the polls in the final month of the midterm elections cycle. To discuss each party's closing strategy, Amna Nawaz sat down with Democratic strategist Faiz Shakir and Republican strategist and media consultant Melik Abdul.

changes.title: Cuban official on Trump's threats as tensions with U.S. rise
changes.summary: For months, the Trump administration has ramped up pressure and threats against Cuba. A de facto oil blockade now means hours of blackouts, plus food and water shortages for millions on the island. While President Trump has threatened a takeover, Cuban officials say they're still willing to talk. Amna Nawaz discussed t.

changes.title: Tamara Keith and Amy Walter on Washington's response to AI and data center concerns
changes.summary: NPR's Tamara Keith and Amy Walter of the Cook Political Report with Amy Walter join Amna Nawaz to discuss the latest political news, including how Washington is responding to AI and data center concerns, Mitch McConnell returning to the Senate and how midterm voters feel about affordability and political corruption.

changes.title: Brooks and Capehart on the GOP's midterm identity
changes.summary: David Brooks of The Atlantic and Jonathan Capehart of MS NOW join Amna Nawaz to discuss the week in politics, including the GOP's midterm convention and the identity of the party, if Democrats should be worried about campaign spending benefiting Republican candidates and how America has changed in the 25 years since 9/.
